- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.8) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.2) or shows sharp drops, model overpredicts; reduce forecast by 1–3% to align with mean reversion bias.
- After a price spike (≥ 5% above recent high), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; cap forecast at +3% above peak or use 20-day moving average.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive within 3 days, model lags; forecast should be adjusted to match sentiment shift within 2–3 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates true price by 1–3% in bullish sentiment periods; apply +1.5% bias to forecast mean.
- If sentiment history shows 3+ consecutive 0.00 values, model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast by 2–4% to avoid overbought bias.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.3–0.7), model often averages out; use sentiment-weighted median of recent 5-day prices to anchor forecast.
